prompt: Compare UCC28C43 and LT3757A current-mode boost controllers at 100kHz for 10.8–13.2V to 170V 2W and a 24V control case. Identify which specs must be confirmed and possible DCM lightweight topologies.
review:
# UCC28C43 vs LT3757A for a 10.8–13.2 V → 170 V, 2 W Boost at 100 kHz (plus 24 V control case)

## 1. Headline comparison

| Parameter | UCC28C43 (TI, BiCMOS UC384x family) | LT3757A (ADI) |
|---|---|---|
| Role | General-purpose current-mode PWM controller (flyback/boost/forward, etc.) | Current-mode boost / flyback / SEPIC / inverting controller, explicitly boost-oriented |
| Supply range (VCC/VIN) | ~7.6–18 V VCC (start threshold ~8.4 V typ, UVLO); not usable at 170 V or 24 V without a pre-reg / bias winding | Wide VIN: nominally 2.9–40 V (check DS for exact min/max and VCC variant) — 10.8–13.2 V and 24 V both inside |
| Gate drive | ~1 A totem-pole, referenced to GND — fine for a low-side N-FET; weak for large Qg at high frequency | Internal N-FET driver, gate current modest (~0.5–1 A class); check under "gate drive" spec |
| Max duty / min off | UC384x-style: duty can approach ~100%; typically needs external slope comp / max-duty clamp; min off-time not explicitly bounded (deadband through timing) | Has a defined maximum duty (~90% class) and minimum off-time (check DS) — important for 170 V step-up ratio |
| Current sense | CS pin, internal blanking (~100 ns typ), leading-edge filter; typical peak-sense threshold ~1 V (check variant) | CS threshold is low (tens of mV class, e.g. ~80 mV); 2 W at 170 V means ~12 mA output, so at 88% duty input current ~200 mA — a very low sense threshold with a small shunt can work, but noise margin at 100 kHz must be checked |
| Frequency | RT/CT programming, up to ~500 kHz–1 MHz depending on variant; 100 kHz easy | Programmable RT; 100 kHz typical range OK — confirm allowed RT range and sync |
| Compensation / dynamics | External COMP; classic Type-II; slope compensation for D > 50% is the designer's job | Built-in slope compensation tied to duty — check amount vs. your inductor/ripple at D ≈ 0.92 |
| Protection features | UVLO, OVP via external, cycle-by-cycle CS, no true soft-start (external) | Has soft-start, OVP comparator input (FBX/FB), programmable current limit — richer built-in protection |
| Output voltage sensing | Needs external divider to a 2.5 V (or similar) reference | Dedicated FB pin with internal reference (check exact value and tolerance) |
| Reference / bias for 170 V | None — must derive VCC from an auxiliary winding or a high-voltage startup/Zener path | Same issue: VIN pins are ≤40 V class, so the 170 V rail must be sensed with a divider and the IC biased from input or an aux winding |

**Bottom line:** For a 2 W, 170 V output at 100 kHz, both are electrically plausible. The LT3757A is the more integrated choice (soft-start, duty clamp, slope comp, current-limit programming); the UCC28C43 is cheaper and simpler but pushes slope compensation, max-duty management, soft-start, and housekeeping for the 170 V sensing onto the designer. Neither IC can be powered directly from 170 V — bias must come from the 10.8–13.2 V input or an auxiliary winding. For the 24 V control case, the LT3757A's wider VIN is a cleaner fit; the UCC28C43 needs the 24 V reduced to its VCC window (e.g., a series Zener/regulator or auxiliary supply).

## 2. Specs that **must be confirmed** from the current datasheets before commitment

1. **Exact UVLO / VCC operating window and start threshold** for the specific UCC28C43 orderable part (UC384x-family thresholds vary by suffix and by vendor; "UCC28C43" TI vs. clone parts differ).
2. **Maximum duty cycle and minimum off-time** on both parts. At 170 V from 12 V, ideal D ≈ 0.93; real D is higher with diode drop. If min off-time × fsw eats the available off-time, DCM/CCM behavior collapses. This is the single most critical check.
3. **Gate-drive capability vs. chosen FET Qg at 100 kHz** (drive current, rise/fall, and thermal). 2 W output does not need a large FET, but gate charge sets drive loss.
4. **Current-sense threshold, blanking time, and leading-edge filter** — especially LT3757A's low CS threshold (noise immunity at 100 kHz with a small shunt) and UCC28C43's ~1 V-class threshold (sense resistor dissipation at ~0.2–0.3 A peak input current is small either way, but blanking vs. spike must be checked).
5. **Built-in slope compensation amount** (LT3757A) and whether it is adequate/not excessive at D ≈ 0.92 with your inductor; for UCC28C43, confirm CS input range and design external slope comp.
6. **Reference voltage, tolerance, and divider loading** on the FB pin; for 170 V, divider leakage
